title: Ike's Morning Digest
data_note: Built from publisher RSS metadata (titles + teaser text). `coverage_window_hours` is the default (40h); several feeds use a longer `rollingHours` (see `scripts/build-digest.mjs`) so rows align with what is still on each publisher’s listing pages. Commercial Observer keeps its retail category + hub supplement; TRD adds a New York–filtered global retail tag feed. PincusCo uses the live site feed only (`/category/retail/feed/` is stale). **CRE Daily** retail briefs come from `credaily.com/sectors/retail/feed/`. **WSJ** is the Dow Jones real-estate feed with lifestyle and opinion dropped. **The New York Times** keeps real-estate and property stories only. **Traded** is commercial deal briefs from its news listing. Open each link for the full article (subscriptions may apply in the browser).

section_overviews.commercial_observer:
Danny Meyer Signs Greenwich Village Lease for New Restaurant: Fresh off his plans to open an eatery at the former Hotel Bossert in Brooklyn Heights, Michelin -star chef Danny Meyer is turning a hungry eye back on Manhattan. Meyer’s Union Square Hospitality Group signed a 10-year, roughly 8,000-square-foot lease at 21 West Eighth Street in Greenwich Village.

Australian Fashion Brand Mode Mischief Inks Lease at SoHo’s 65 Spring Street: Australian fashion brand Mode Mischief has signed a 2,000-square-foot retail lease at 65 Spring Street in Manhattan’s SoHo, Commercial Observer has learned. The deal converts the spot where the apparel company has held a pop-up location since May into its permanent home for the next five years.

Kids Art Studio ColorPop Workshop to Open at Tribeca’s 450 Washington Street: A pop of color can certainly brighten your day. ColorPop Workshop , an art studio offering children ages 3 to 12 a variety of classes, has inked a 1,000-square-foot deal at the base of Related Companies ’ 450 Washington Street in Manhattan’s Tribeca neighborhood, according to tenant broker Meridian Retail Leasing .

Williamsburg Secures Highest Retail Asking Rent in Brooklyn in 2026: REBNY: Williamsburg remains the shopping capital of Brooklyn. A flurry of leases and rising rents have defined the area in 2026, according to the Real Estate Board of New York (REBNY) ’ s most recent Brooklyn retail report, shared exclusively with Commercial Observer.

The property is owned by Grace Jean , tenant broker TSCG — formerly known as The Shopping Center Group — confirmed. The deal was signed Oct. 15.…

items.headline: Houston Retail Demand Tops New Supply for First Time in a Year
items.summary: Houston retail net absorption of 399,400 SF beat 339,800 SF of deliveries in Q3, the first quarter in 12 months in which demand topped new supply, according to Colliers. Rents rose 7.9% to $22.06 per SF, a fourth straight record, and sales volume climbed 18% to more than $953M, though vacancy edged up to 5.8% and leasing slowed. Construction jumped 48% to 4.4M SF, so a new supply wave could test a market where restaurant, fitness, medical and grocery demand is well diversified.…

items.headline: Australian Fashion Brand Mode Mischief Inks Lease at SoHo’s 65 Spring Street
items.summary: Australian fashion brand Mode Mischief has signed a 2,000-square-foot retail lease at 65 Spring Street in Manhattan’s SoHo, Commercial Observer has learned. The deal converts the spot where the apparel company has held a pop-up location since May into its permanent home for the next five years. The asking rent was $575 per square foot, a source close to the deal told CO. Current Real Estate Advisors ’ Oded Nachmani represented the brand in this deal, which takes effect in January.…

items.headline: JLL: Retail Vacancy Dips to 4.3% as Openings Beat Closures
items.summary: U.S. retail net absorption totaled 8.3M SF in Q3 after 10.2M in Q2, and vacancy slipped to 4.3%. Over 12 months the market absorbed 24.4M SF, versus a 7.0M SF loss a year earlier. Discount, off-price, grocery, fitness and entertainment tenants are backfilling boxes left by the 2024-2025 bankruptcy wave, often at higher rents. Net new supply is only 0.25% of inventory. Asking rents are up 1.8% against 3.7% inflation.…

items.headline: Thor Equities Buys San Francisco Office and Retail Building for $51M
items.summary: Thor Equities Group is doubling down on San Francisco, particularly in its Union Square district. The New York-based real estate investment firm has acquired a 136,714-square-foot office and retail building at 55 Stockton Street for $50.55 million, Commercial Observer can first report. Property records show Zaber Corporation previously acquired the property in October 2016. Prime Finance provided $51.8 million in acquisition financing for 55 Stockton.…

items.headline: Namdar Takes Control of Destiny USA’s $430M Mall Debt
items.summary: Namdar Realty Group, a Long Island firm known for distressed retail, acquired the debt on Destiny USA, New York’s largest shopping center, and is now lender of record in bond filings. Pyramid Management Group failed to close a bid to buy the $430 million CMBS for under 20 cents on the dollar, and the top tranche now trades near 17 cents.…

items.headline: Outdoor Apparel Brand Kühl to Open First NYC Store at 520 Fifth Avenue
items.summary: Baby it’s cold outside, so you better bundle up with outdoor gear from New York City’s latest retail addition. Utah-based outdoor apparel brand Kühl is set to open its first store in New York City at Rabina ’s 520 Fifth Avenue in Midtown, the real estate investment and development firm announced this week.…

items.headline: Fifth Avenue Retail Rents Jump 35% to Top Global Rankings
items.summary: Upper Fifth Avenue retail rents rose 35% year over year to an average of $2,700 a square foot, the highest in the world, per Cushman & Wakefield. Availability on upper Fifth dropped 4.4 percentage points to 13% in Q3, and brands such as Meta, Prada and Kering have made big commitments. The rebound mirrors a wider Manhattan recovery in office rents and hotel rates, and demand has spread to lower Fifth Avenue.…

items.headline: Hudson River Trading Expands to 551K SF at 3 World Trade Center
items.summary: Hudson River Trading (HRT), a leading electronic and quantitative trading firm, has added a large chunk of office space to its global headquarters at 3 World Trade Center . HRT, which moved into its Financial District home in 2018, just signed a lease to add 340,000 square feet to its existing 211,207-square-foot office at 175 Greenwich Street , according to landlord Silverstein Properties . The new expansion brings HRT’s total footprint at 3 World Trade Center to approximately 551,207 square feet.…

items.headline: Miami Investor Buys Fort Lauderdale Retail Center for $35M
items.summary: Core Investment Management has paid $35.4 million for a strip mall in Fort Lauderdale, following a four-year repositioning. The 73,756-square-foot asset called Gateway Shopping District features 11 buildings between 1914 and 1980 East Sunrise Boulevard . The strip mall is sandwiched between 18th Northeast Avenue and 20th Northeast Avenue, near the 799,851-square-foot Galleria Mall , which is slated to be redeveloped into a mixed-use development.…

items.headline: Moinian Group Modifies 2 Washington Street’s $131M CMBS Loan, Secures New Tenant
items.summary: What started with a tenant bankruptcy has evolved into a much happier ending for Moinian Group ’s 2 Washington Street in Battery Park City, and just in time for the holidays. The $131 million commercial mortgage-backed securities (CMBS) loan on the building, which was previously leased to the now-bankrupt hospitality company Sonder , has been successfully modified, and Moinian Group has signed a new, similar tenant in Prism , sources familiar with the situation told Commercial Observer.…

items.headline: Los Tacos No. 1 to Open at 900 Third Avenue in Midtown East
items.summary: A popular Mexican street taco chain in New York City is opening yet another location in Manhattan. Los Tacos No. 1 , which debuted at Chelsea Market in 2013, has signed a 15-year, 7,105-square-foot lease at the base of Elecor Properties ’ 900 Third Avenue in Midtown East, according to landlord broker Cushman & Wakefield . The taqueria’s new spot on the corner of Third Avenue and East 54th Street will open in mid-2027 and replace a shuttered Bank of America branch.…

items.headline: London Jazz Club Inks 12K-SF Lease at 250 Mercer Street in NoHo
items.summary: It’s just a noisy hall where there’s a nightly brawl, and all that jazz . Famed London jazz club Ronnie Scott’s has signed a 20-year, 11,739-square-foot lease at 250 Mercer Street in Manhattan’s NoHo neighborhood. Ronnie Scott’s opened in 1959 in London’s Soho district and was the first U.K.-based club to regularly host American jazz legends such as Ella Fitzgerald and Miles Davis. Now, the business plans to build out a premier jazz club on Manhattan’s Mercer Street, in what will be its first U.S. location.…
